title: DailyMed lithium carbonate prescribing information
support: Diuretic-associated sodium loss can reduce lithium clearance; hydrochlorothiazide is a listed example. This supports the interaction, not an invented medication chronology.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Fresenius Kabi potassium chloride concentrate label
locator: Dosage and administration; adverse reactions (including infusion discontinuation)
support: This product requires dilution. For potassium above2.5mEq/L its label specifies at most10mEq/hour and40mEq/L; site reactions include phlebitis/extravasation and warrant discontinuation/evaluation. Product-specific labeling does not establish a universal peripheral ward concentration limit.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Royal Children’s Hospital: Pyloric stenosis
support: Correct dehydration/electrolyte disturbances before surgery; add potassium only after urine output is adequate. The guideline supplies1–2mL/kg/hour as its adequacy criterion.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia: Pyloric stenosis
support: Feeds can begin a few hours after surgery, with small increasing amounts of Pedialyte or direct breastmilk/formula. A universal clear-liquid-first12–24-hour rule is not supported. Search-index text verified; direct open returned an error.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Kesin lactulose solution prescribing information
support: Excessive dosing can cause diarrhea with fluid/electrolyte losses. Dose reduction and discontinuation for persistent diarrhea contradict a universal never-stop instruction; clinician-directed adjustment remains required.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: DailyMed spironolactone prescribing information
support: Aldosterone antagonism promotes sodium/water excretion while retaining potassium; it does not support the item’s claim that spironolactone predictably worsens potassium depletion.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: DailyMed morphine sulfate tablets prescribing information
support: Morphine acts at opioid receptors and can depress respiration, including brainstem response to carbon dioxide. This label does not establish two exclusive dyspnea-mechanism distractors or guarantee absence of respiratory adverse effects.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Scottish Palliative Care Guidelines: Breathlessness
support: Guidance describes carefully titrated opioids for refractory breathlessness, including heart-failure contexts; dosing must consider prior exposure and renal function. Used to ground a replacement symptom/monitoring construct, not import a dose.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: NIA: Advance care planning and advance directives
locator: Living will versus durable power of attorney
support: A living will specifies treatment preferences; a durable healthcare power of attorney names a proxy. Merely documenting an advance directive with a daughter present does not establish her appointment.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: HHS: Communication with family and others involved in care
support: With a capable patient present, relevant information may be shared if the patient agrees or does not object; professional judgment and best-interest provisions also exist. Emergency-contact status is not unlimited disclosure authority. A proposed permission-based response is one valid path, not the sole legal path.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: MedlinePlus: Poisoning first aid
support: Assess airway/breathing and protect against aspiration; side positioning during vomiting supports the airway-priority proposition. This does not replace emergency clinical assessment.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: EXTRIP Workgroup lithium recommendations
support: Decreased consciousness, seizures or life-threatening dysrhythmias can justify extracorporeal treatment independent of lithium concentration. The systematic recommendation is also indexed at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25583292/; clinical evidence quality is low.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: ASCO/IDSA outpatient fever and neutropenia guideline2018
support: Published oral fever thresholds pair38.3°C with101°F for one reading and38.0°C with100.4°F sustained one hour. Preserve the published pairing for the case’s call rule; distinguish clinical thresholds from ordinary measured-temperature conversions.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Endotext: Treatment of thyroid storm
support: The specific dependency is iodine after the first thionamide dose (one hour); glucocorticoids are part of concurrent treatment. A forced four-drug total order placing STAT steroid last is not established.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: NICE CG84: Gastroenteritis in children under5
support: Assess dehydration using the full clinical picture; worsening responsiveness and perfusion are important red flags. Oral rehydration is appropriate in many dehydrated children. Isolated absent tears does not itself establish shock or exclusion of oral rehydration.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: NICE CG32: Adult nutrition support
support: Unsafe/inadequate oral intake with a functional accessible gut can support enteral tube feeding. PN indications concern inability to meet needs safely by oral/enteral routes or gut dysfunction. Inability to swallow alone does not prove that all enteral feeding is impossible.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate prescribing information
support: Altered consciousness, impaired gag reflex and regurgitation increase aspiration risk. This supports querying oral resin in the documented lethargic patient without inventing current vomiting.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: CDC: Recommended actions based on blood lead level
support: A confirmed venous10–19µg/dL result follows an early1–3-month retesting schedule with exposure/nutrition/development management. Capillary confirmation follows a different schedule. The≥45µg/dL lane calls for specialist-directed chelation consideration.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: ACOG: Preeclampsia and high blood pressure
support: Severe blood pressure and neurologic/organ features can signal preeclampsia, including postpartum. HELLP denotes hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets; a subset of those findings is not the complete triad.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Jakafi prescribing information
locator: Acute GVHD indication and safety monitoring;14.3
support: Ruxolitinib is used for steroid-refractory acute GVHD with hematologic/infection monitoring. Explicit symptom/laboratory direction can be interpreted without extrapolating an8-hour stool amount to a24-hour total. No new dose is proposed.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: DailyMed clozapine prescribing information
support: Suspected myocarditis warrants discontinuation and cardiac evaluation; it commonly occurs early in treatment. ANC/fever management must follow the applicable population-specific labeling and the case’s stated hold protocol. Current label is used without relying on obsolete REMS assumptions.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: KDIGO2012 AKI guideline
support: AKI care includes continued creatinine, urine-output and hemodynamic assessment. Improved vitals do not discharge monitoring needs. KDIGO’s live AKI page states the2026 revision is preparing for publication after public review; a draft is not substituted for final guidance.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: SCCM/IDSA: New fever in critically ill adults
support: Simultaneous central and peripheral cultures support differential time-to-positivity assessment; the same organism appearing centrally at least two hours earlier supports a catheter source. An unspecified earlier bottle alone does not establish that criterion.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: AHA: Tachycardia
support: Resting adult tachycardia is above 100 beats/minute. A rate of 92 alone does not support calling the rhythm sinus tachycardia.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: AHA2025 special circumstances of resuscitation
support: Support airway and ventilation promptly; naloxone complements resuscitation and may require repeated doses. The recommendations do not establish a rigid total ordering of concurrent team tasks.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: AHA2025 Adult Advanced Life Support
locator: 10: Vasopressor medications in cardiac arrest; cardiac-arrest algorithm
support: Prioritize CPR and defibrillation in shockable arrest; epinephrine is reasonable after initial defibrillation attempts fail. Preparing medication can occur alongside other team work; preparation is not administration.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign2026 adult guideline
support: Collect blood cultures as soon as possible, ideally before antimicrobials. Sepsis/shock requires immediate treatment and resuscitation; a rigid cultures-first key must not license avoidable treatment delay or treat a single marker as exclusion of infection.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: UKKA acute hyperkalaemia guideline, updated July2026
support: Resin therapy has limitations in acute hyperkalaemia and is not a substitute for immediate cardiac protection and potassium shifting. UK recommendations distinguish CPS from US SPS; the SPS label independently grounds aspiration risk. No UK dosing protocol is imported into the US case.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: HHS: Breach notification rule
locator: Risk assessment; administrative requirements and burden of proof
support: Breach response requires assessment, mitigation and documentation under institutional procedures. This page does not authorize a bedside nurse to permanently delete potential evidence before privacy review; that unprovided procedure remains a review hold.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: HHS: Workers compensation disclosures
support: Workers-compensation disclosures have legally defined permitted pathways; a general no-disclosure-to-employer claim cannot replace assessment of authority and scope.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: HHS: Incidental uses and disclosures
support: A limited incidental disclosure can be permitted when the underlying communication is permitted and reasonable safeguards are applied. Overhearing is not automatically a violation independent of context.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Aphasia Institute: Capacity and decision making tools
support: Communication support can help people with aphasia understand and express decisions. Aphasia alone does not establish incapacity; an assessment and authorized surrogate relationship cannot be inferred from inability to speak.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: AMA Code of Medical Ethics: Informed consent
support: Assess understanding, implications and ability to make a voluntary decision; communicate options and document consent. Emergency exceptions and surrogate decisions depend on their specified conditions, not merely a signature or a family presence.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: HHS: Family or friend as interpreter
support: For important decisions, interpretation must be accurate, effective and impartial. Family may lack competence or have conflicting interests. The provider must offer competent services at no cost when needed for meaningful access; a patient can decline the provided interpreter.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: ACC: Cardiogenic shock and mechanical circulatory support2025 review
support: Hemodynamic assessment guides vasoactive support and escalation; the consensus favors norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor. Choice of inotrope/vasopressor depends on the clinical profile; a universal immediate-inotrope rule needs review.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: ASPEN Consensus Recommendations for Refeeding Syndrome
support: Phosphorus, potassium and/or magnesium decline and associated organ dysfunction within five days of calorie reintroduction support refeeding syndrome. A concurrent infectious process is not excluded by that diagnosis. Detailed treatment doses require full guideline review; none are proposed here.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS: SBAR
support: Structured handoff includes current situation, pertinent background, assessment and a request/recommendation. Case-specific data must be actually available at the selected boundary; later completed calls cannot supply those facts retroactively.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS: Teach-back
support: Ask the patient or caregiver to explain needed information/actions in their own words. A chart title announcing success/failure can give away the interpretation being tested.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: CDC: CAUTI summary of recommendations
support: Acute urinary retention can be an indication for catheterization; unnecessary use should be avoided. A patient-specific retention/fall-risk assessment supports assisted care, not a universal catheter-first or walking-toilet rule.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: CDC: Transmission-based precautions
support: Gown/gloves are used for interactions involving contact with the patient/environment, with appropriate removal and hand hygiene. Case-specific caregiver knowledge must be assessed rather than inferred from a later demonstration.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: International Pressure Injury Guideline: Heels
support: Select and check heel-offloading devices; periodically remove them to assess skin, perfusion and swelling. A shifted device can create new pressure even when a heel remains intact; the current skin/device assessment matters.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: NIA: Caregiver worksheets
locator: Coordinating responsibilities; home safety; medication management
support: Care planning includes shared caregiving responsibilities, home safety and medication oversight. An individual caregiver’s resource needs still require the actual case assessment, not generic dementia facts.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: SAMHSA SAFE-T
support: Suicide assessment includes direct inquiry about ideation, plans, behavior and intent, risk/protective factors, intervention and documentation. A denial of current thoughts is not documentation of a separately asked plan/intent assessment.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: SAMHSA: Opioid overdose prevention and reversal
support: Emergency response, breathing/resuscitation support and an available opioid reversal medicine are essential. Extra opioid doses and combinations with sedatives/alcohol increase risk; naloxone access does not replace treatment continuity and monitoring.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Joint Commission: Suicide risk reduction
support: Mitigate patient-specific environmental risks, use one-to-one observation where indicated and remove potential self-harm objects when this does not undermine medical care. The case must establish which equipment is removable and how essential care continues.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: National Capital Poison Center: First aid
support: Collapse, seizure, breathing difficulty or inability to awaken requires emergency services. Other exposures merit immediate poison-expert advice; do not induce vomiting. This supports clear triage wording without generating a new pediatric drug dose.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Buprenorphine/naloxone sublingual film label
support: The described16mg/4mg maintenance target is a single daily dose with individualized prescribing. A morning dose already taken plus an unexplained second full evening dose conflicts with the case’s once-daily regimen; reconcile the medication timeline, not invent a new regimen.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Genentech Activase prescribing information
support: The label identifies pretreatment INR greater than1.7 as a reason to discontinue treatment and requires blood-pressure monitoring/control. The case’s institutional rule remains a necessary visible input where the question explicitly asks to apply that rule.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: DailyMed nicardipine hydrochloride injection
support: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate continuously during infusion and avoid excessive/rapid pressure reduction. A later achieved pressure or completed medication preparation cannot be used as an earlier nursing decision cue.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: SITC immune-checkpoint adverse-event guideline2021
locator: Hepatitis recommendations; corroborating SITC2017 diagnostic evaluation
support: Checkpoint therapy can cause colitis/hepatitis, but competing causes of liver injury require evaluation. The2017 SITC consensus explicitly includes viral infection, alcohol, medications and cancer progression: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5697162/. Existing liver metastases cannot be silently excluded.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: NICE NG232: Head injury
locator: Referral; CT criteria; deterioration and transfer
support: New neurological deficits, reduced consciousness and concerning vomiting after injury require prompt evaluation/escalation. The proposal uses observed post-fall findings; it does not introduce a new local transport or CT protocol.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: NHS: Broken hip
support: Hip/groin pain with an abnormally angled or shortened leg after a fall raises fracture concern and needs hospital assessment. Such findings should not be treated as merely routine follow-up or resolved by walking the patient.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: NICE NG234: Metastatic spinal cord compression
support: Cancer with new neurological or bladder dysfunction can indicate a spinal cord emergency; prompt specialist management and corticosteroids are recommended in the appropriate setting. The case’s newly prescribed IV medication is a real stage-specific input; a bladder scan after no void is not a postvoid residual.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.

title: Australian Red Cross Lifeblood: TACO
support: Post-transfusion respiratory deterioration with hypertension, positive fluid balance and cardiac involvement supports circulatory overload. Baseline risk factors alone do not establish the actual reaction; consider the current cluster and competing transfusion reactions.
limitations: Supports the stated clinical premise, not the producer visibility verdict or any unreviewed rewrite.
